title: ErrorProblemDetails
description: The document a service sends when an operation fails: an RFC 9457 problem detail whose errors member carries the classified errors. Served as application/problem+json, which is how a client tells it from a gateway's error page.

type.description: The problem type. Always about:blank, since this contract identifies a problem by the kind and code of its errors rather than by a documentation URI.

title.description: A short summary of the error kind. Describes the type rather than the occurrence, and is not localised — render from a code instead.

status.description: The HTTP status of the response, mirroring the status line. Taken from the first error's kind.

detail.description: The first error's message, when it has one. Never the text of an unhandled exception.

instance.description: The request path. Never includes the query string.

errors.description: The classified errors, most significant first. The first one decides the status and title.

kind.description: What class of thing went wrong. Normally one of the sixteen below; a service may report a kind of its own, so treat this as an open set and fall back to the status.

code.description: Which specific error it was. The key a client renders text from, so a catalogue needs an entry for every code a service can send, including the per-kind defaults in error-kinds.json.

message.description: A description for whoever reads the response directly. Present but often empty. Neither localised nor stable, so never parse it and never show it to an end user.

payload.description: The parameters of the error: the values a client substitutes into the text it renders for the code, such as the offending field or a limit that was exceeded. Keys are sent exactly as the service wrote them.
